title: High Blood Pressure
text: Blood pressure is recorded as two numbers. A normal reading is below 120/80 mm Hg. Elevated blood pressure is a systolic (top) number of 120 to 129 with a diastolic (bottom) below 80. Stage 1 high blood pressure is 130 to 139 systolic or 80 to 89 diastolic; stage 2 is 140 or higher systolic or 90 or higher diastolic.

title: High Blood Pressure
text: The DASH eating plan can help lower blood pressure. It emphasizes fruits, vegetables, whole grains, and low-fat dairy, and it limits sodium, red meat, sweets, and saturated fat. Cutting back on sodium lowers blood pressure in many people.

title: Cholesterol
text: LDL is often called the bad cholesterol because a high LDL level leads to a buildup of plaque in the arteries. HDL is called the good cholesterol because it helps carry cholesterol back to the liver. A high LDL level raises the risk of heart disease and stroke.

title: Cholesterol
text: High blood cholesterol means there is too much cholesterol in your blood. It usually has no symptoms. Over time it can cause plaque to build up in the arteries, narrowing them and raising the risk of heart attack and stroke.

title: Cholesterol Medicines
text: Statins are the most common medicines used to lower high cholesterol. Lifestyle changes such as a healthy diet, regular exercise, and not smoking are also important, and medicine is often combined with these changes.

title: Cholesterol
text: A blood test called a lipid panel measures total cholesterol, LDL, HDL, and triglycerides. Adults have their cholesterol checked periodically; your provider decides how often based on your risk factors.

title: Diabetes
text: Type 2 diabetes is the most common form. The body still makes insulin, but the cells do not respond to it well, so glucose builds up in the blood. It can often be delayed or prevented with a healthy diet, a healthy weight, and regular physical activity.

title: Diabetes
text: People with diabetes have a higher chance of heart attack and stroke. Controlling blood sugar, blood pressure, and cholesterol, and not smoking, are important for lowering that risk.

title: Diabetes
text: Physical activity helps control diabetes by lowering blood glucose and helping insulin work better. Drink plenty of water before, during, and after exercise, and check your blood sugar as your provider advises.

title: Healthy Sleep
text: Most adults need 7 or more hours of good-quality sleep on a regular schedule. Not getting enough sleep raises the risk of health problems and affects how the body repairs itself and fights infection.

title: Healthy Sleep
text: To sleep better, go to bed and wake up at the same time each day, avoid caffeine in the afternoon and evening, avoid nicotine, and exercise regularly but not too close to bedtime.

title: Exercise and Physical Fitness
text: For substantial health benefits, adults should do at least 150 minutes a week of moderate-intensity aerobic activity, plus muscle-strengthening activities on 2 or more days a week.

title: Benefits of Exercise
text: Regular physical activity can help control weight, lower blood pressure and cholesterol, and reduce the risk of heart disease, stroke, and type 2 diabetes. It also improves mood and energy.

title: Flu
text: The best way to prevent the flu is to get a flu vaccine every year. The flu can be serious, and it can make chronic health problems, such as asthma, worse.

title: Heart Disease Prevention
text: You can lower your risk of heart disease by not smoking, controlling blood pressure and cholesterol, keeping blood sugar in range, eating a healthy diet, staying active, and keeping a healthy weight.

title: COPD
text: COPD (chronic obstructive pulmonary disease) is a long-term lung disease that makes it hard to breathe. The most common cause is smoking. Symptoms include a cough, wheezing, and shortness of breath.

title: Nutrition
text: Food gives you the energy and nutrients you need to be healthy. Eating a variety of foods and balancing the calories you take in with the ones you use helps you stay at a healthy weight.

title: Fitness and Exercise
text: If you are starting to exercise, begin slowly and build up over time. Warm up before and cool down after activity, drink water, and choose activities you enjoy so you keep them up.
